title: Cognee: knowledge-graph memory for agents
by: Topoteretes' open-source Python library. Read from the repo via raw.githubusercontent.com: the README, the package's public exports (cognee/__init__.py), the improve() orchestrator and its docstring, and the conflict models. Then from docs.cognee.ai: the llms.txt and llms-core.md indexes, Remember, Improve and Forget (core-concepts/main-operations), Review Conflicting Facts (guides/review-conflicts), Resolve Conflicting Facts (guides/resolve-conflicts) and Memory Provenance (guides/memory-provenance).
summary: Cognee turns text, code and conversations into a knowledge graph plus vector index that agents search. The API is four verbs: remember, recall, improve and forget (older: add, cognify, memify, search; memify is now legacy). improve() runs nine stages in a fixed order; each one gates, and the result reports every stage as completed, already_completed, skipped with a reason, or errored. Its conflict review, on by default, uses a model to find facts that disagree across dated sources, stores each disagreement as a FactConflict, and marks the facts current, superseded or conflicting. A person settles what the review cannot with resolve_conflict(), giving a reason. Forget is a hard delete.
ideas: Four verbs: remember, recall, improve, forget. remember() without a session_id runs the whole pipeline into a named dataset; with one it writes to a fast session cache, and a background improve() bridges it into the permanent graph unless self_improvement=False.

improve() runs nine stages in a fixed order (feedback_weights, persist_session_qa, persist_agent_traces, extract_agent_context, distill_sessions, update_user_preferences, build_truth_subspace, review_conflicts, global_context_index). Each gates first and reports skipped with a reason such as no_session_ids, opt_in_disabled, turned_off or no_llm_configured.

Fail open except where loss is real: a stage failure is recorded and the next stage runs, but a failure to persist session Q&A stops the run, and an exhausted LLM budget marks every later stage skipped with budget_exhausted. A failed trace pass is rolled back whole and its watermarks do not move.

Conflict review: only facts that could disagree go to the model, each with the date its source holds as of (effective_date in the item's metadata). Each accepted disagreement becomes a FactConflict node linked to the entity, the competing values and the source chunks; the facts get marks: current, superseded or conflicting.

A fact that never changes (where a company was founded) cannot be settled by date, so it stays unresolved. resolve_conflict(conflict_id, dataset_id, selected_fact_id, reason) records the choice; the other facts stay as superseded, recall applies the choice at query time, and later automatic reviews keep it while the chosen fact exists.
Watermarks: the review re-reads only entities whose facts changed since the last run. A rerun over unchanged data reports already_completed and makes no model call.

forget() deletes for real: one item, a dataset or everything a user may delete, across graph, vector and relational stores. It also drops cached session answers built on what it removed. memory_only=True clears only graph and vector data so the dataset can be rebuilt.

Provenance: get_memory_provenance_graph() and visualize_memory_provenance() show ownership and flow (tenant, user, agent, dataset, file) from the relational database; include_memory links extracted entities back to their files. The code also takes one lock per dataset, so improve, cognify, add and forget on one dataset run one after another.

took.idea: A conflict record that names the attribute, whether it can change over time, the candidate docs, and marks each one current, superseded or conflicting
A person's choice on a conflict, with its reason, that later automatic runs keep
Separate a session's scratch notes from brain, and move only accepted lessons over in one explicit step
Fixed, gated stages that report skipped with a reason, never silently
An honest outcome per write run: failed, noop or done
A watermark, so a rerun over unchanged docs does nothing and says so
One writer at a time per area
